title: Gideon and the Visitor
premise: Mirabel Nystrom, an urban explorer obsessed with documenting the unmapped tunnels beneath her dying mill town, is the first to witness what the excavation crew unearths: a door sealed from the inside, humming with a song no one remembers learning. The door's keeper — Gideon, a man who has guarded it for longer than he can account for — insists she leave before the frost inside finishes writing its pattern on the walls. But Mirabel's documentation has already woken something, and the only way to close the breach is to learn the song's final verse without ever singing along. In the end, Mirabel chooses loyalty to Gideon over duty to the town that sent her down, singing the verse with him as the frost completes itself — sealing them both inside a door that now opens onto nothing, together.
about_author: Petra Whitlock is the pen name of a former municipal archivist who spent a decade cataloguing basement records in northern industrial towns before turning to horror. She writes about people who believe that naming and recording a thing can keep it at bay — and about the moment that belief fails.

chapters.title: Everything Is a Kind of Prayer
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She maps a storm drain system off-survey beneath Harrow Mill, photographing, sketching, logging coordinates with ritual precision. She finds a wall of frost where no pipe runs cold. Emotional beat: the comfort of obsession, and the first hairline crack of wrongness.

chapters.title: The Crew Breaks Ground
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The redevelopment crew's bore hits a void; she talks her way onto the site by offering her survey data. They pull up a slab of black stone with a ring handle. Emotional beat: vindication curdling into dread when the crew chief admits the tunnel isn't on any record he's ever seen.

chapters.title: Sealed From the Inside
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Examination of the door reveals hinges fused, bolts thrown from within, and frost blooming outward from its seams in deliberate, geometric patterns. Her camera captures a sound like humming. Emotional beat: awe — she has never documented anything this beautiful or this wrong.

chapters.title: Gideon
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A man appears at the site after hours — calm, weathered, calling himself Gideon, demanding they cover the door again. He speaks of the frost 'writing' and warns her that her photographs are pages in someone else's book. Emotional beat: suspicion; he knows too much to be a crank.

chapters.title: The Song Under the Town
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. That night she hears the melody through her floorboards, three verses long, ending mid-phrase. Her recordings of the tunnels contain the same tune underneath the water noise. Emotional beat: compulsion — she catches herself humming and stops, frightened.

chapters.title: What the Archive Won't Say
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Digging through county records, she finds Gideon's name on a 1911 excavation permit — same face in the photograph. A marginal note reads 'keeper, do not relieve.' Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery giving way to the weight of knowing.

chapters.title: Duty Calls It an Anomaly
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The company brings in engineers who declare the door structurally inert and schedule demolition. Gideon begs Mirabel to destroy her documentation instead. Emotional beat: torn between the truth she owes the world and the warning she owes him.

chapters.title: Frost Patterns
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The frost on the door has spread into legible script — names, hundreds, each one crossed out. The last name is half-written and uncrossed. Emotional beat: cold clarity; this is a ledger, and something is still writing in it.

chapters.title: The Demolition
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Mirabel and the site foreman. The crew's first strike cracks the door; the humming becomes audible to everyone; two workers walk into the tunnel and don't come out. Emotional beat: panic and guilt — Mirabel realizes her published photos drew the crowd that made this possible.

chapters.title: Inside
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Searching for the missing workers, she crosses the threshold. Inside: a corridor of frost-script, warm air moving like breath, and Gideon waiting, furious and afraid for her. Emotional beat: crossing over — there is no undocumented way back.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Confession
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He explains his bargain: he holds the door because the thing behind it trades silence for songs, and every verse sung aloud gives it a voice. He has forgotten everything except the song and his post. Emotional beat: loneliness laid bare — a century of duty with no one to share it.

chapters.title: Two Workers, One Verse
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She finds the missing men deep in the corridor, mouths moving, eyes frosted, singing the third verse perfectly. One dies when she pulls him free; the other lives but cannot speak. Emotional beat: grief and resolve — the song takes what it teaches.

chapters.title: Documentation Is Not Protection
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Back home, she reviews her footage and finds frames she never shot: herself asleep, filmed from inside the wall. Her archive has become the entity's memory. Emotional beat: betrayal by her own faith — recording has fed it.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He offers to wipe her memory of the tunnels so she can be free, as he once offered another, long ago — the half-written name on the door. She refuses. Emotional beat: tenderness sharpened into defiance; she will not be erased to be saved.

chapters.title: The Company Seals the Site
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Authorities pour concrete over the entrance with workers still unaccounted for, declaring the matter closed. The frost begins appearing in Mirabel's apartment, writing on her windows. Emotional beat: claustrophobic abandonment — the town chooses ignorance, leaving her alone with the truth.

chapters.title: The Fourth Verse
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He admits there is a final verse he has never taught anyone: the one that ends the song instead of continuing it. Singing it requires a second voice in harmony — which is why he was always alone, and why he could never finish. Emotional beat: hope arriving disguised as sacrifice.

chapters.title: Learning Without Singing
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Gideon teaches her the last verse note by note; she may hum it only in thought, lips sealed, while the frost on her windows transcribes every mistake. Emotional beat: disciplined intimacy — two people bound by a rule neither can break alone.

chapters.title: The Frost Writes Its Final Pattern
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The script completes itself across the town — windows, ice, breath on glass — and the entity's voice arrives wearing the dead foreman's tone, offering Mirabel her own name back if she sings the third verse instead. Emotional beat: temptation at its most personal.

chapters.title: The Door Opens Both Ways
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. Mirabel returns to the threshold; Gideon stands ready to sing his part. Together they begin the fourth verse — harmony, not solo — and the corridor of frost-script burns blank behind each line. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into trust.

chapters.title: Sealed From the Outside
chapters.summary: Climax continued, Mirabel's POV. The song ends; the entity, given no solo voice to take, collapses into silence. The door swings shut — bolted now from their side. Emotional beat: triumph inseparable from loss; the seal requires a keeper, and there are two.

chapters.title: A Door That Opens Onto Nothing
chapters.summary: Resolution, Gideon's POV. Beyond the sealed door lies not a prison but a small warm room with two chairs, a lamp, and Mirabel's recovered notebooks — every page blank except the ones she wrote by hand. Emotional beat: quiet peace; found family in the smallest possible house.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Epilogue, framed as Mirabel's final journal entry, left where explorers will find it. She documents the door, the rule, the song's danger, and signs off: some things should stay mapped and unopened. Emotional beat: bittersweet closure — her prayer answered, her archive ended on purpose.
